summary: Albany County Fasteners (legal entity Raw Products Corp) is a family-run fastener distributor that started in a two-car garage in 2010 and now runs a 25,000 sq ft warehouse in Edison, NJ stocking 40M+ pieces, selling online to both B2B and B2C customers with piece/pack/bulk pricing and no order minimum. Orders come in through a self-serve Shopware web store plus phone, email and Tawk.to live chat during weekday 8-5 hours; quotes, NET 30 credit, kitting and certification documents are handled by a small in-house sales team. Public reviews praise selection, price and shipping speed but flag packaging and order-recovery handling, and the company is mid-expansion (new racking, poly-bagging equipment, replatformed site).

facts.fact: Founded in 2010 in a two-car garage in New York State; main 25,000 sq ft warehouse is at 100 Newfield Ave, Suite D, Edison, NJ 08837, with 40M+ fasteners in stock shipping worldwide.
Sells nuts, bolts, screws, washers, rivets, anchors and accessories in piece, pack or bulk with no order minimum and volume discounts; serves both B2B and B2C customers.
Most orders ship within 24 hours and many same day, primarily via UPS, with Second Day/Overnight options, customer UPS account billing, local pickup in Edison and international shipping.

Legal entity is RAW PRODUCTS CORP D/B/A AlbanyCountyFasteners.com; the company publishes a quality policy with objectives of 95%+ satisfaction and an order error rate below 0.5% of shipped orders per quarter.
Business hours are Monday-Friday 8:00AM-5:00PM EST; phone 866-573-0445, email and web contact at 100 Newfield Ave, Suite D, Edison, NJ 08837.

Robert (Bob) Cominos is President and owner; wife Anna is Vice President, son Peter is Purchasing Manager, Francesca is Warehouse Fulfillment Manager and Victoria is Brand, Marketing and HR manager; the company says its family team has grown to over 20 employees.
The company says it uses a smart, AI-powered Warehouse Management System for real-time inventory, automated workflows and faster fulfillment.

B2B services include custom quotes for listed and unlisted products, USA sourcing, custom manufacturing, C of C/MTR/shop drawings on request, blanket release and stock-and-lock programs, and an online NET 30 credit application.
Most orders ship same day, otherwise within 24 to 48 hours, and shipped orders generate an email notification with tracking data.
Review aggregator Birdeye shows a 4.6-star rating across 429 reviews for the Edison location (profile not claimed by the business).
Yelp listing shows 2.5 stars from 21 reviews, with review text praising selection, pricing and fast shipping while complaining about packaging and order resolution.
The company also sells through an Amazon storefront and publishes educational fastener content on a blog and a YouTube channel with about 39,300 subscribers and 353 videos.

operations_signals: Order intake is self-serve web checkout on the company store, backed by a toll-free line (866-573-0445), email, a quote request form and a Tawk.to live-chat widget; no online appointment or service booking exists (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/Contact-Us/).
Coverage is Monday-Friday 8:00AM-5:00PM EST only, with no weekend or published after-hours support for phone/chat leads (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/Customer-Service/About-Us/).

Fulfillment promise is same-day or 24-hour shipping on most orders, a triple quality check and custom packaging on every order; local pickup and van delivery are offered from the Edison warehouse (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/Customer-Service/About-Us/).

B2B quote requests and documentation requests (C of C, MTRs, shop drawings) go to a human sales team, including quotes for unlisted and custom-manufactured items (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/B2B/Request-A-Quote/).
NET 30 credit terms require an online application before qualified accounts can order on terms (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/B2B/Request-A-Quote/).

The FAQ routes customers who need to change quantities or edit an order to contact the team for immediate assistance, and directs order-status questions to the account portal or shipment email (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/Customer-Service/FAQs).
Shipping confirmation, tracking and order history are self-service in the customer account portal, while exceptions depend on staff (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/Customer-Service/FAQs).
hiring_signals: No careers page exists on the company site (Careers and Customer-Service paths return 404) and no current openings surfaced on Indeed, LinkedIn or ZipRecruiter results, so hiring appears to run through informal or third-party channels (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/Careers/).

Public LinkedIn profiles show a small in-house team covering warehouse order processing, purchase/fulfillment analysis, quality control and IT/SEO, plus an executive assistant to the CEO - roles that carry repetitive order, purchasing and QC coordination work (https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-o-loughlin-319893118).

A buyer/purchasing-and-fulfillment analyst role indicates manual purchasing and inventory analysis is done by a named individual rather than a large planning team (https://www.linkedin.com/in/jessica-gottmann-296243190).

A public Facebook jobs-group post advertised a Machine Operator role at Raw Products Corp in Sayreville, NJ alongside a warehouse associate-type role referencing Albany County Fasteners; the post date is unclear (https://www.facebook.com/groups/phillyjobs/posts/3185101041576764/).

Warehouse fulfillment, purchasing, and brand/marketing/HR functions are each held by one family member, which concentrates scheduling and admin work in a few people (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/blog/about-albany-county-fasteners/).
review_themes: Positive: broad selection of hard-to-find stainless/brass/silicon-bronze fasteners, low prices and fast delivery, with repeat buyers describing years of ordering (https://local.yahoo.com/info-195846697-albany-county-fasteners-edison/).

Packaging complaints recur: hardware arriving in bags or cardboard envelopes rather than sturdy boxes, with reviewers noting the trade-off against low prices (https://local.yahoo.com/info-195846697-albany-county-fasteners-edison/).

Service-recovery complaints: one long-time customer says management 'refused to make good' on an issue and made the vendor a last resort; a forum thread describes not getting a response to a paid order (https://local.yahoo.com/info-195846697-albany-county-fasteners-edison/).

Ratings diverge sharply by platform - 4.6 stars over 429 reviews on Birdeye/Google versus 2.5 stars over 21 reviews on Yelp - so complaint concentration is likely age- and channel-specific (https://reviews.birdeye.com/albany-county-fasteners-171344557997627).
An aggregator summary of customer feedback highlights prompt delivery and dependable service alongside the product range (https://albany-county-fasteners.wheree.com/).
tech_footprint: Storefront runs on Shopware 6 (Shopware theme tokens and CMS element markup in page source), with custom homepage/category CSS maintained in-house (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/).
Live chat is Tawk.to, toggled from the header navigation and footer (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/).
Yotpo review widget loader and Google Tag Manager (GTM-WFNJ3R) are installed on the storefront (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/).
Customer account portal provides order history, tracking and NET 30 application status hooks (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/Customer-Service/FAQs).

Second sales channel via an Amazon storefront; payments include major cards, PayPal, PayLater and Apple Pay plus NET 30 for approved B2B accounts (https://www.amazon.com/stores/AlbanyCountyFasteners/page/7B1D54CC-242B-4E4F-A20A-CE6E32705A64).
Tiered bulk pricing is configured in the platform, and a downloadable 2024 line card PDF is published for B2B buyers (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/B2B/Request-A-Quote/).

Content operation spans a blog (Fasteners 101 guides) and a YouTube channel with roughly 39.3K subscribers and 353 videos, including warehouse and product explainers (https://www.youtube.com/albanycountyfasteners).
growth_signals: Grew from a two-car garage in 2010 to a 25,000 sq ft Edison warehouse with 40M+ pieces in stock; earlier company descriptions cited 18M pieces, implying inventory roughly doubled (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/Customer-Service/About-Us/).
Company video announces a move to a bigger warehouse with new, larger racking installed to add space for more inventory and line expansions (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FAyagUQ6bBU).
Added poly-bagging machines and custom packaging/kitting capability, shown in a warehouse walkthrough video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YZClmlBQi00).
Replatformed/rebuilt the web store, promoted with a 'new website tutorial' video emphasizing a streamlined ordering process (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3mQeK6xVqQw).

Company LinkedIn describes Albany County Fasteners as a 'multi-million dollar fastener super store', indicating scale well beyond the original garage operation (https://www.linkedin.com/company/albany-county-fasteners).

Site now carries dedicated shipping/support landing pages for six U.S. regions (Midwest, Northeast, Southeast, South, Mountain, West) plus a nationwide page, pointing to a national-demand SEO build-out (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/fasteners-nationwide).
decision_maker: Robert 'Bob' Cominos, President and Owner - listed on the company's own blog page 'About Albany County Fasteners' (https://www.albanycountyfasteners.com/blog/about-albany-county-fasteners/); Anna Cominos is Vice President and Peter Cominos is Purchasing Manager on the same page

inferences.inference: Quote and RFQ handling is the most human-bound workflow and a strong AI-agent target.
inferences.reasoning: The company advertises quotes for listed and unlisted products, USA sourcing, custom manufacture, C of C/MTR/shop drawings and stock-and-lock programs, all handled by a sales team of a ~20-person company - each quote needs product lookup, pricing tiers and document assembly.

inferences.inference: Inbound inquiries outside 8-5 EST go unanswered until the next business day, creating a lead-capture gap for a nationwide, all-50-state customer base.
inferences.reasoning: Published hours are Monday-Friday 8-5 EST with no stated after-hours coverage, while the site markets shipping to all 50 states and internationally.

inferences.inference: Post-order support (edits, address changes, WISMO, damage/packaging claims) is a recurring cost driver.
inferences.reasoning: The FAQ tells customers to contact the team to edit orders, and public reviews repeatedly raise packaging quality and unresolved order issues rather than product quality.

inferences.inference: Catalog and order-data accuracy is a structural bottleneck worth automating.
inferences.reasoning: 40M+ pieces across many grades/materials, piece-pack-bulk tier pricing, and a self-imposed sub-0.5% order error target mean product data and picking accuracy carry high stakes for a small staff.

inferences.inference: Key-person dependency is high because purchasing, fulfillment, QC and marketing each map to a single named individual.
inferences.reasoning: The company's own About page assigns each function to one family member, and LinkedIn shows single named holders for buyer/purchasing analyst and QC lead roles.

inferences.inference: They are receptive to automation and already invest in it, which lowers adoption friction for agent tooling.
inferences.reasoning: They publicly describe an AI-powered WMS, run poly-bagging equipment, replatformed their store, and maintain an IT/SEO specialist role.

data_gaps: No public careers page (site /Careers and /Customer-Service paths return 404) and no verifiable current job postings - hiring volume and role mix are unconfirmed.
BBB business profile returned HTTP 403, so accreditation status, rating and complaint counts could not be verified (a search snippet indicated 'Not BBB Accredited').
Yelp, Glassdoor and Indeed pages returned HTTP 403; review themes rely on Yelp excerpts syndicated via Yahoo Local and a Birdeye rating shell, not full review text.
Employee count ('over 20') comes only from the company's own blog; no independent headcount or revenue figure was retrievable (Craft.co, ZoomInfo and CB Insights pages blocked or paywalled).
No local news or trade-press coverage of the expansion was found; the warehouse move and poly-bagging investment are documented only in company videos.
An Instagram post referenced 'new precision capabilities coming soon' but the page could not be opened, so the claim is unverified and excluded from growth signals.
Job-board coverage (Indeed, ZipRecruiter, LinkedIn Jobs) could not be read directly due to bot blocking, so absence of open roles is not confirmed.
